sources.edition: Introduction à la vie dévote, texte de 1619 établi par Fernand Boulenger, Paris: Garnier, 1909 (original spelling, modernized only in typography). Proofread transcription on French Wikisource (validated, category "Bon pour export"), taken from the "Texte entier" page.
sources.description: Francis's text with Boulenger's footnotes, kept as markdown footnotes. Boulenger's front matter (Mgr Baunard's letter, the introduction "La Philothée de Saint François de Sales"), the lexicon and the table of contents are not included.
sources.tierEvidence: Francis died in 1622; Boulenger's edition was published in 1909 (public domain in the US, published before 1930) and Boulenger died in 1934, so his notes are public domain in France too (life+70, since 2005). Wikisource's transcription is CC BY-SA, but the underlying text is public domain.
Anonymous nineteenth-century translation; CCEL marks it Public Domain.
sources.edition: Introduction to the Devout Life, anonymous translation, Rivingtons edition (CCEL e-text).

description.fr-FR: Le guide de saint François de Sales (1608-1609, texte définitif de 1619) pour mener la vie chrétienne au milieu du monde : cinq parties de conseils et d’exercices, écrits pour Philothée, qui veut aimer Dieu dans sa condition ordinaire.
description.en-US: St. Francis de Sales's guide (1609; definitive text 1619) to living a devout life in the midst of the world: five parts of counsels and exercises written for Philothea, who wishes to love God in her ordinary state of life. The original French is Boulenger's edition of the 1619 text; the English is an anonymous nineteenth-century translation.
description.pt-BR: O guia de São Francisco de Sales (1609; texto definitivo de 1619) para viver a vida devota no meio do mundo: cinco partes de conselhos e exercícios escritos para Filoteia, que deseja amar a Deus em seu estado de vida comum.
